topic: How does L-DACS integration impact spectrum sharing between A2G and satellite links in congested airspaces?
consensus_response: The integration of L-DACS1 and L-DACS2 in congested airspaces presents a complex challenge for spectrum sharing between A2G and satellite links. L-DACS1, operating in full duplex with FDD, offers robust performance but may introduce significant interference due to simultaneous frequency usage. L-DACS2, with its TDD and half-duplex approach, reduces interference but limits capacity. Satellite links, providing broader coverage, introduce high delays and Doppler shifts, complicating spectrum management. To address these challenges, a hybrid approach combining the strengths of both L-DACS1 and L-DACS2, as well as 5G and Wi-Fi technologies, can provide a robust and flexible solution. A centralized control entity (CCE) will manage resource allocation, synchronization, and interference mitigation, ensuring seamless communication among different technologies. Advanced AI and ML algorithms can optimize resource allocation and interference mitigation, but lightweight and efficient implementations are essential. Close collaboration with regulatory bodies and standardization organizations is necessary to ensure alignment with existing regulations and standards.
